answer: Each epoch poses a fresh task seeded by a randomness beacon no one can foresee, like a trellis whose shape is redrawn every round. A sybil cannot pre-compute replies from an atlas of cached answers, nor mirror one identity's work across many, because every address draws distinct required words and each answer-hash must be unique. Unpredictable, machine-checked prompts force real per-identity labor, so cloned accounts have nothing to copy.
